hints: Notice you are given frequency $f = 6.7 \times 10^{14} \text{ Hz}$ in vacuum and lines per metre $N = 4.0 \times 10^{5} \text{ m}^{-1}$, so first find wavelength $\lambda = c/f$ and slit spacing $d = 1/N$.
Recall normal-incidence grating maxima satisfy $d \sin\theta_n = n\lambda$, so write this separately for $n = 2$ and $n = 3$ with your $d$ and $\lambda$.
Calculate $\theta_2 = \sin^{-1}(2\lambda/d)$ and $\theta_3 = \sin^{-1}(3\lambda/d)$, then subtract to get the angle between the two adjacent maxima.
walkthrough: Find the wavelength in vacuum from $c = f\lambda$. $\lambda = c/f = (3.00 \times 10^8)/(6.7 \times 10^{14}) \approx 4.48 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$.
Find the grating spacing from lines per metre. $d = 1/N = 1/(4.0 \times 10^5) = 2.5 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}$.
Use $d \sin\theta_n = n\lambda$ for normal incidence. For $n = 2$, $\sin\theta_2 = 2\lambda/d \approx 0.358$, so $\theta_2 \approx 21.0^{\circ}$.
The angle between the two directions is $\theta_3 - \theta_2 \approx 32.5^{\circ} - 21.0^{\circ} \approx 11.5^{\circ}$, about $12^{\circ}$. This is option A.

options.B: This is approximately the angle of the second order maximum $\theta_2$ from the central maximum, not the separation $\theta_3 - \theta_2$.
options.C: This is approximately the angle of the third order maximum $\theta_3$ from the central maximum, not the separation $\theta_3 - \theta_2$.
options.D: This is approximately the sum $\theta_2 + \theta_3$, whereas the question asks for the difference between the two directions.
